narrative:
The model estimated a 95.8% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, and that high-risk prediction is why your law school application was rejected. This is not a certainty, but it means the model found your profile much closer to students who failed than to students who passed.

The strongest factor was your third-year academic standing: you were in the lowest decile, far below the average of about 5.79 among accepted students, and this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor was your first-year standing: being in decile 2, compared with an accepted-student average near 6, also pushed toward failure. Third was your LSAT score of 28, below the accepted-student average of about 37.18; this pushed toward failure too, though less than your class standing.

To move forward, ask admissions whether reconsideration or an appeal is available and request feedback on your file. Consider intensive LSAT preparation and a retake, and take additional academic coursework or a structured law-school preparatory program to demonstrate readiness. Meet with a pre-law advisor to build a stronger application, and look for schools that use holistic or conditional admission review.
